result.explanation: The conditional rule is: callbacks affect state only when the controller is mounted, still loading, and the callback ID equals the current request ID. A new search cancels the prior loading request before issuing its request; disposed instances ignore everything except mount.
result.mapping: The rule maps request identity and lifecycle state to visible state transitions and ordered effects: current identifies the sole settleable request, loading gates settlement, mounted gates all activity, and effects records only cancellations and requests from the current event.
result.assumptions: Events use the documented types and fields. State is trusted only as the state previously returned by this function; null means the documented initial mounted state. JSON values are finite and directly reusable.
result.holds: function holds(input,output){function eq(a,b){if(a===b)return true;if(!a||!b||typeof a!==typeof b)return false;if(Array.isArray(a))return Array.isArray(b)&&a.length===b.length&&a.every((v,i)=>eq(v,b[i]));if(typeof a==='object'){let ka=Object.keys(a),kb=Object.keys(b);if(ka.length!==kb.length)return false;return ka.every(k=>Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(b,k)&&eq(a[k],b[k]))}return false} let s=null,r=[];for(let e of input.events){let x=solve({config:input.config,state:s,event:e});s=x.state;r.push(x.output)}return eq(r,output)}
